name: north-south scrap metal fence section seen from above as a band: top edge of the sheets and post heads, tiles into a vertical line
label: wasteland_ruins/fence-v

surfaces.part: metal sheet band (teal/grey strip running the full height)

answer.evidence: The object is a narrow vertical band, 8-9 px wide and 16 rows tall. It is the top edge of the sheets seen from above, tiled vertically. The main band (x=7: rows 0-1, 6-9, 14-15) has no front face and no front-edge line with an eave shadow. The two brown post heads (rows 2-5 and 10-13) each have a 1-row light line, 2 brown rows and a dark row. They are only 4 rows tall, and they are small details on the band, not a south face under a top surface. The main body therefore has no front face of 3 or more rows and is a flat top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow vertical band of stacked scrap sheets and post heads, a sparse prop like the lamp and bench references. On the primary facts it is at or above the references. It has 15 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. Its near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. Its dark edge pixels are 0% near-neutral, so the outline is tinted. By eye the darks lean brown and blue-grey beside the metal and rust, not black, so I read the outline as dark material tone. Each material shows about 4 lightness steps (highlight, mid, dark, rust or edge), slightly fewer than Beodeul's 5-6, but the per-sheet variation and patching give enough grain that it would sit acceptably next to the hedge and bench. It is not sticker-like.

surfaces.part: sheet band (top edge of the scrap sheets, seen from above as a vertical strip)

answer.evidence: The main body is a narrow vertical band 8-9 px wide and 16 rows tall. The column scan shows no front face under it, only a lighter blue-grey strip at x=5-7 and a darker strip at x=9. Silhouette width stays at 8-9 for every row. It reads as a plan view of the fence, not an upright frame with horizontal beams and a base. The only elevation cues are two small post-head blocks at rows 2-5 and 10-13. Each has a 1-row tan top (L=180), 2 rows of brown face and a 1-row dark shadow. These are details and do not make a 3+ row front face for the main body. The kind is frame, so beams and a base should show top faces with a front below, and this drawing has neither.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow vertical band, so I judged it mostly from the measured facts and could only partly check it by eye. It has 15 visible tones per 16x16 tile, which sits between prop-hedge (9) and prop-well-roofed (20) and is close to prop-stall-cheese (17). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%, so the outlines carry a tint (brownish/rusty beside the metal and posts) rather than being a black sticker line. Sheet tops and post heads show about 4-5 value steps with some grain and variation. Since the references are about 9-20 tones, it does not look thinner or flatter than they do. The weak point is that the band is small and I could not confirm per-sheet highlight detail by eye.

answer.evidence: The main body is a narrow vertical strip about 8-9 px wide and 16 rows tall. It is drawn as a flat band seen from above, with the sheet columns running top to bottom and no south-facing front face. The two brown blocks at rows 2-5 and 10-13 each have a tan top line (rows 2 and 10), 2 rows of face and a dark base row. They are small details, not the main volume. Nothing shows a front-edge line with a tall front face below it, and the strip has no legs or apron. It matches the 'top-down slab (no front)' reference, not an open frame with beams and base showing top faces.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin vertical band, so I judged it mostly by eye plus the measured facts. It reads as stacked sheet segments and post heads, with about 5 lightness steps across its metal and wood-like tones. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted and follows the adjacent material instead of being a uniform black sticker line. It has 15 visible tones per 16x16 tile and 0% near-flat coverage. That is above prop-hedge (9) and close to prop-stall-cheese (17) and prop-well-roofed (20). The segments carry some variation and grain rather than flat fills. It is a little simpler than the richest references, but a careful artist would accept it beside them without it looking flatter or more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: scrap sheet band (metal, teal-grey, runs the full height)

answer.evidence: The object is an 8-9 px wide vertical strip over 16 rows. The sheet band (rows 0-15, columns x=7 and x=9) is a continuous top-down band with no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no south face below it. The two brown post heads (rows 2-5 and 10-13) each have a 1-row tan highlight at row 2 or 10, 2 rows of brown at rows 3-4 or 11-12, and a dark row at row 5 or 13. That is a small block detail, not a horizontal surface over a front face. There is no base, no horizontal beam top and no legs, so the main body has no front face of 3 or more rows and it is a flat top-down slab. It does not read as a frame with a top surface and a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical band of stacked sheet tops and post heads, in grey-brown metal and rust tones. It measures 15 visible tones per 16x16 tile, above prop-hedge (9) and close to prop-stall-cheese (17) and prop-well-roofed (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills of 5x5 or larger. The dark edge pixels are 0% near-neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark tone of the adjacent material rather than a black sticker line. Each sheet shows about 4-5 value steps, with highlight, mid, dark and rust or shadow variation. That is slightly under Beodeul's 5-6 steps, but the grain varies from sheet to sheet.
